clue.text: Lady-killer cautious about destiny with detective or prosecutor

indicators.note: one word placed about the rest goes round them, enclosing them

blocks.note: chary means wary or cautious
your lot is your fate in life
TEC is short for detective
taken as written
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A woman who murders men hedges about her fate, with a detective or a prosecutor on her trail.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything after 'about' sits inside the cautious word. Charlotte Corday stabbed the French revolutionary Marat in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a lady who killed someone, the theme's reading of lady-killer rather than its usual sense of a womaniser.

clue.text: One's through keeping the noise of a little beast from the birds

indicators.note: the noise a word makes is how it sounds when spoken, so we want a word sounding like the beast
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: one is A; the 's is 'has'
via means by way of, through
a fawn is a young deer; a faun is the goat-legged woodland god

explanation.surface: Someone passing through holds on to a small animal's cry, away from the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The little beast is a young deer, but its sound-alike is the goat-legged woodland god of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective term for all bird species living in a particular region or period.

clue.text: The first princess in Egypt

blocks.note: A is the first letter, as in A1 or grade A
Princess Ida is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera and Tennyson's poem

explanation.surface: Who was the earliest royal daughter in ancient Egypt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Egypt' completes the whole clue as a definition: Verdi's heroine is an Ethiopian princess held captive in Egypt, and the opera was first staged in Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Verdi's opera is a captured Ethiopian princess enslaved at the Egyptian court.

clue.text: Sailors detained by policeman, one having a loaf in America

indicators.note: someone detained by another is held in custody, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: a cop is a policeman
RN is the Royal Navy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seamen are arrested by an officer, one of them idling in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a loaf' suggests lazing about, but loaf here is bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn pone is a simple bread baked from cornmeal, typical of the southern United States.

clue.text: Distinguish between rings set in Cyprus

indicators.note: a piece placed between others ends up enclosed by them

blocks.note: to tell apart is to distinguish
rings are round, each like the letter O

explanation.surface: Tell the difference between jewellery rings mounted on the island of Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like it belongs with the rings, as a jewel is set, but it begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera based on Shakespeare's Othello takes place in Cyprus, so it is a work whose action is located there.

clue.text: Money for old-fashioned disciplinarians

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for pounds or dollars
second meaning: people who punish children with a slap

explanation.surface: Payment to stern teachers of the old school.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackers is slang for currency units, and taken literally it names people who smack, the old style of punishing children.

clue.text: Scottish novelist's 4half way home

indicators.note: only half of the cross-referenced entry is kept, the rest is dropped
a different way of putting something suggests rearranging these letters

blocks.note: the answer to 4-down
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer's midway house.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints '4half' run together and the clue seems slightly garbled; the likely reading takes CORN, the first half of 4-down, rearranges it, and adds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Cronin was a Scottish doctor and novelist, author of The Citadel and creator of Dr Finlay.

clue.text: Building material in the country may cause fractures

blocks.note: first meaning: what rough rural huts are put up from, the sticks also meaning the country
second meaning: from the rhyme saying these may break my bones

explanation.surface: Rural construction supplies can lead to broken bones.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me'; 'the sticks' is also slang for remote countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are crude rural building stuff, and the playground rhyme says they can break bones.

clue.text: Discuss thoroughly and take the dentist's advice?

blocks.note: first meaning: settle a dispute by arguing it fully
second meaning: a dentist might tell you to get a bad tooth removed

explanation.surface: Thrash things out and do what your dentist recommends.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to confront a disagreement openly; literally it is having something extracted, like a tooth.

clue.text: 1 did in combination of parent with deserter

blocks.note: ma is mother
a rat deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Someone murdered by a mix of mother and turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did in' means killed: 1-down, Charlotte Corday, stabbed this French revolutionary in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was the revolutionary journalist whom Charlotte Corday murdered in 1793, so he is her victim.

clue.text: Don't sing the chorus

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, hold back from doing
second meaning: a noun, the repeated lines of a song

explanation.surface: An instruction not to join in singing the chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sing' joins the two meanings; the surface reads as a single order.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to abstain, the sense of 'don't'; as a noun it is a repeated section of a song.

clue.text: Wasting few words on Tory layabout?

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

blocks.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy
Con is short for Conservative
the printed word is split in two: its first half is the lay piece and its second half the container signal

explanation.surface: A lazy Conservative who barely says a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layabout' must be split into two words: lay, then about.
explanation.definitionFit: A laconic speaker is terse, using very few words to express something.

clue.text: Piece of round matter

blocks.note: O is round in shape
pus is the matter in an infected wound

explanation.surface: A portion of something spherical.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a numbered musical work or composition, a piece in the musical sense.

clue.text: 21 did in eagles' vac

blocks.note: vac and hol are both short for holiday
the possessive reads as 'of eagles', and an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: Someone killed during the eagles' holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'eagles' vac' as 'vac of eagles': HOL, OF, ERNES. In the Apocrypha Judith (21-down) beheads the Assyrian general Holofernes.
explanation.definitionFit: Holofernes is the general whom Judith decapitated to save her city, so he is her victim.

clue.text: Slice round 14's head during unconsciousness

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
something during something else happens within it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a trance is a state of unawareness
14-across is Holofernes

explanation.surface: Cut round the head of Holofernes while he lies senseless, as Judith did.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface retells the story: Judith beheaded the drunk, sleeping Holofernes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or part of something larger, as in a tranche of funding.

clue.text: Talk loudly about West Bromwich Albion's recovery?

indicators.note: one thing placed about another surrounds it

blocks.note: to clack is to chatter noisily
WBA is the standard abbreviation of the English football club

explanation.surface: Fans loudly discussing a football club's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: West Bromwich Albion is an English football club; 'recovery' suggests a sporting comeback but means getting money back.
explanation.definitionFit: A clawback is the recovery of money already paid out, such as tax or bonuses reclaimed.

clue.text: Republican supporter from ancient 26?

blocks.note: first meaning: a man for George Bush, the Republican president
second meaning: a member of an ancient people of southern Africa (26-across)

explanation.surface: A backer of the Republican party with roots in old Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it is a supporter of the Bush presidents; whole, it names the San hunter-gatherer people of southern Africa.

clue.text: Little tub for one given a degree by university in Georgian city

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
taken as written
Bath, famed for its Georgian architecture, has a university

explanation.surface: A small tub, for a graduate of a university in a Georgian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' seems to point at a person, but the one is an infant. Bath is an English spa city of Georgian terraces.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby bath is a small plastic tub for washing an infant, a vessel sized for a single small child.

clue.text: Soviet politician, a man, king in a month

indicators.note: a piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a man is a male
NOV is the calendar abbreviation for November
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A Russian statesman, an ordinary man who becomes king for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgy Malenkov briefly succeeded Stalin as leader of the USSR in 1953.

clue.text: Temporary employment for patient fellow in leisure wear

indicators.note: a person in clothing is wrapped by it, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: casuals are informal clothes
the Biblical Job is proverbial for patience

explanation.surface: Short-term work for a long-suffering man dressed informally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' suggests a hospital, but it means long-suffering, as in the patience of Job.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual jobs are short-term or irregular positions without a permanent contract.

clue.text: 25 did in relation to time

blocks.note: sis is short for sister, a relation
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone killed in connection with a period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in relation to' looks like one phrase but splits. In the Book of Judges Jael (25-down) drives a tent peg through the Canaanite general Sisera's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisera is the commander whom Jael killed with a tent peg, making him her victim.

clue.text: Lady-killer in hospital after project embracing princess

indicators.note: something embracing another wraps its arms round it, so it encloses it

blocks.note: to jut is to stick out, project
Di was Diana, Princess of Wales
H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: A woman who kills lies in hospital after a scheme that involved a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts H at the end. Judith is the Apocryphal heroine who killed Holofernes.
explanation.definitionFit: Judith beheaded the general Holofernes, so she is a lady who killed, the theme's sense of lady-killer.

clue.text: More could follow 11

blocks.note: first meaning: in addition, extra
second meaning: the number eleven itself, not the cross-reference

explanation.surface: Further lines could come after the chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 looks like a reference to 11-across, but it is the number: the eleven-plus was the British exam taken at age 11 to decide secondary schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means additional or extra, and it completes the name of the old British school selection exam.

clue.text: English girl with American man, one might gather

blocks.note: Rose is a girl's name, and the rose is England's flower
bud is an American way of addressing a man

explanation.surface: An English girl with an American man, as one might infer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one might gather' sounds like 'I suppose', but echoes Herrick's line 'Gather ye rosebuds while ye may'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herrick's poem urges young people to pick these unopened flowers while they can.

clue.text: Good heavens, my jo! No doctor in the house?

indicators.note: 'no' a thing means without it, so those letters are taken away
a piece in another sits inside it

blocks.note: 'House!' is the winner's cry at bingo, once called housey-housey
taken as written; jo is Scots for sweetheart
MO is a Medical Officer

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise to a sweetheart: is there no doctor in the house?
explanation.walkthrough: 'No doctor' strips the medical officer's letters from 'my jo', and the remainder goes inside the house. 'My jo' is from Burns's song John Anderson, my jo.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, the old-fashioned oath matching the expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Lady-killer in prison said yes to the translations

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want a word as it sounds

blocks.note: a jail is a prison
a confirming second route rather than extra letters: German JA for yes, then Spanish EL for the

explanation.surface: A murderess behind bars agreed to the translations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yes to the translations' gives a second wordplay: JA is German for yes and EL Spanish for the. Jael killed Sisera with a tent peg in the Book of Judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Jael slew the general Sisera, so she is a woman who killed, the theme's sense of lady-killer.

clue.text: One day short for a hundred: the poet''s continent

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end

blocks.note: one is A
FRI is the abbreviation for Friday
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: One day short of a hundred, as a poet might describe a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'day short' gives the shortened form of a weekday. Poets such as Milton used the clipped form for Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Afric is an archaic, poetic shortening of the name Africa, the continent.

clue.text: Newspaper with part of 3, 5 and 21 in 13s, perhaps

definitions.text: Newspaper with part of 3, 5 and 21 in 13s, perhaps

blocks.note: in publishing a newspaper is a title
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A newspaper with a share of several entries in musical works.
explanation.walkthrough: 13s are opuses, here operas: Aida, Otello and Judith (Honegger's) are each named after the lead character.
explanation.definitionFit: A title role is the part of the character a work is named after, like Aida in Verdi's opera.
